newsitem.title: CHINA: China shows "iron fist" in amphibious war games.
newsitem.headline: China shows "iron fist" in amphibious war games.

text.p: China said on Sunday it had staged amphibious war games that signalled a turning point in its ability to land forces on distant shores aided by the "iron fist" of its armoured units.
The war games combined air, sea and land forces in a recent, successful assault on an unspecified island, according to the Liberation Army Daily.
"Our armoured units have become the iron fist of our landing assault capability," said the armed forces newspaper.
It did not identify the military units that took part or say where the exercises were held but it added that warships steamed in formation "over long distances" before the assault was made.
The report made no mention of any potential target.
China held unarmed missile tests and war games near Taiwan in a bid to intimidate the island ahead of presidential elections in March this year.
China views Taiwan as a rebel province and has not renounced the use of force to regain the island, separated from the mainland by some 150 miles of the Taiwan Strait.
U.S. military analysts have said they do not believe China will have the ability to mount an assault on Taiwan for several years.

The newspaper said the war games made use of tanks, armoured personnel carriers, artillery and infantry to storm and hold a beachhead while anti-tank and other weapons were fired at defending "enemy" forces.
"In the future our forces will have the ability...to make a rapid amphibious attack using heavy firepower and protected by effective covering fire in a modern landing assault," the newspaper said.
